name: VAT return
legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. 22(1): "A taxable person shall, in respect of Value Added Tax (VAT), with or without a notice and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, submit a return to the Service in the prescribed form, on or before the 21st day of the following month"; s. 22(3): "the returns shall contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and Value Added Tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month." A tax period is one calendar month, and no cadence but monthly exists for it — unlike Belgium or Ireland, nothing in the Act lets a taxable person ask for a longer one. **The return is filed on the Service's own portal, TaxPro-Max, which has accepted no manual VAT return since June 2021** (Federal Inland Revenue Service Information Circular on e-filing, June 2021); the most recent public specimen of a printed form this pack's research could find is Form VAT 002, whose worked example still carries the 5% rate the Finance Act 2019 superseded and whose figures are stated inclusive of VAT in a way TaxPro-Max's own sales-schedule upload (net value entered, VAT computed at 7.5%) does not appear to reproduce. Rather than transcribe a paper form's box numbers as if they were what the portal shows today, this pack numbers its own boxes against the statutory description of s. 22(3) — output tax, input tax, VAT payable — the way packs/sa/tax_report.json numbers a return that is itself a screen and not a printed form. A reviewer who files a real return on TaxPro-Max should check the boxes against what the portal shows.

deadline.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. 22(1), quoted above. Section 49(1) sets the same day for payment: "every person shall make payment of tax due on or before the due date of filing", and s. 154(4), for VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted by a government body or an appointed collector, gives the fourteenth day instead — a different obligation on a different person, which this pack does not model (packs/ng/README.md).

boxes.name: Standard-rated sales
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 147: taxable supplies at the standard rate of 7.5%, stated net of the tax itself under s. 148(1)(a).

boxes.name: Output VAT on standard-rated sales
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. 22(3): the output tax collected on taxable supplies.

boxes.name: Zero-rated sales
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 186: exported goods, services and incorporeal property, and the domestic supplies the section lists — basic food, medical and pharmaceutical products, educational materials, agricultural inputs, electricity supplied to or by the national grid, medical services and equipment, and tuition.

boxes.name: Exempt sales
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 185(1): oil and gas exports, crude petroleum oil and feed gas, land and buildings, money and securities, government licences, and the other items of that section.

boxes.name: Total output tax
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. 22(3), the "output tax collected" component of the return.

boxes.name: Standard-rated domestic purchases
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 155(4): input tax deductible on a taxable supply, including services and fixed assets, to the extent used in making taxable supplies.

boxes.name: Deductible input VAT on standard-rated domestic purchases
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 155(4), the deductible input tax of a standard-rated domestic purchase.

boxes.name: Zero-rated purchases
boxes.legal_reference: A purchase of a supply section 186 rates at zero percent, carrying no input tax to deduct.

boxes.name: Exempt purchases
boxes.legal_reference: A purchase of a supply section 185 exempts, carrying no VAT at all.

boxes.name: Imports of goods
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 149: the value of an imported taxable supply, plus non-VAT duties and charges and the costs of getting it to the port or point of entry.

boxes.name: VAT paid to the Nigeria Customs Service on import, deductible
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 155(3): an importer pays the VAT on taxable goods to the Service, in practice through the Nigeria Customs Service, before clearing them; the tax is then deductible under s. 155(4) like any other input tax.

boxes.name: Total input tax deductible
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, s. 22(3), the "input tax paid" component of the return.

boxes.name: VAT payable, or refundable
boxes.legal_reference: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, s. 155(1): where output VAT exceeds input VAT the excess is remitted to the Service; where input VAT exceeds output VAT the taxable person carries the excess forward as a credit against subsequent months, or under s. 155(2) may request a refund. This pack applies no floor at zero: a negative figure here is the credit or the refund s. 155 describes.
